title: Quentin and the Harbor
premise: In 1913, Quentin Marsh arrives in a fog-bound harbor town carrying letters written in the hand of Edith Amberdale — a woman officially drowned seven years ago. Hazel Amberdale, who has secretly read every letter she's ever delivered for her suffragist employer, recognizes the handwriting as her presumed-dead sister's and realizes her family's survival was built on a staged death. As the morning tide approaches, one berth remains on a ship that can carry only one of them out before the authorities close in. Quentin must choose between saving Hazel, who holds the truth, or the sister whose return would shatter everything — and he gives the berth to Hazel, choosing the living future over the ghost of the past.
about_author: Ines Coldharbour spent a decade cataloguing maritime archives along the northern coast, where she first encountered records of women who vanished into new lives. She writes historical fiction about the quiet bargains people make to survive.

chapters.title: The Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Quentin Marsh, a courier paid to ask no questions, delivers a letter bearing the unmistakable hand of Edith Amberdale — dead these seven years. Hazel Amberdale intercepts it at her employer's house, recognizing her sister's script, and confronts him. POV alternates between Quentin and Hazel. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance forged in shared shock; the corpse has begun writing again.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Careful Silence
chapters.summary: Hazel reveals what she knows: Edith faked her drowning to escape a scandal that would have destroyed the family, and Hazel has guarded the silence ever since. But the new letters demand money and passage, and someone else has been reading them too. POV: Hazel, with flashbacks. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into fear as inheritance and identity begin to unravel.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Quentin traces the letter-writer to a harbor boarding house and finds not Edith but a blackmailer impersonating her — yet the real Edith is alive, hiding nearby, watching. Confronted, she offers Quentin a bribe to deliver one final letter naming which Amberdale sails on the morning ship. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: climax; the price of survival made literal in a single berth.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At dawn, Quentin gives the berth to Hazel, sending her toward a new life while Edith chooses to stay and face exposure on her own terms rather than run again. The blackmail collapses; the family inherits its truth instead of its shame. POV: Hazel, watching from the deck. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity reclaimed, but at the cost of the family she knew.
